description.narrative: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

title.narrative: Improving Access to Quality Education in Yemen - School Doors

description.narrative: (Yemen): ...The Improving Access to Quality Education in Yemen- I (IAQY - I) activity is part of the USAID School Doors program. It works through the Ministry of Education (MOE) to strengthen and institutionalize non-formal education programs as a viable pathway for out-of-school children (OOSC), allowing them to resume their education. IAQY-I increases access to safe and quality education through improved service delivery at local and community levels and will expand equal access to an education that meets the needs of crisis-affected OOSC in Sana'a, Hodeidah, and Al Dhale governorates... ..FY 2019 funded activities include:.. ..- Establishing or reactivating Father-Mother councils for parental and community engagement in schools; developing school improvement plans; distributing teaching and learning kits to teachers and students respectively; and conducting back-to-school campaigns; .- Training and support to teachers on aspects of instructional quality and pedagogy, as well as school safety and psychosocial support; .- Providing children with effective psycho-social support through daily social-emotional learning activities; and .- Developing and establishing guidelines and protocols for community schools to incorporate them into the formal education system including technical assistance on financial and human resource management, procurement, information systems, peer-to-peer networks, and creating policy for accreditation and eventual integration. . Activities will result in restoring education opportunities for OOSC by increasing access to safe and quality education and expanding equal access to education to meet the needs of crisis-affected children. This directly contributes to objective 1 of the USG Education strategy: Expand access to quality basic education for all, particularly marginalized and vulnerable populations...

description.narrative: (Yemen): With FY 2024 funds, the Peace and Inclusive Political Processes in Yemen Program will partner with the Republic of Yemen Government (ROYG) and allies to support its efforts to govern more effectively and responsively and to function as a more productive interlocutor in peace and political processes. The program will also strengthen the capacity of Yemeni civil society, with a particular focus on youth and the private sector, to partake in consensus-building efforts and to meaningfully participate in the public life of Yemen. Finally, the Program will support the safe and meaningful participation of women in both the ROYG and civil society organizations (CSOs) in governance, peace, and political processes, including in leadership positions. .Key interventions will include advancing results-driven dialogue among government and civil society; fostering consensus-based dialogue among political actors; providing training and capacity building opportunities to enhance government effectiveness, oversight, and accountability; fostering networking, relationship-building, and advocacy across different groups; and supporting gender-sensitive policy development. As a whole, these interventions strengthen governance and advance a more inclusive and durable peace process in Yemen. ..

description.narrative: (Yemen): Yemen faces one of the world's most severe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) crises. Inadequate WASH access fuels the spread of cholera and diarrhea, worsening malnutrition in a country with high levels of food insecurity and stunting, while also complicating efforts to control other communicable diseases. Females are particularly affected due to their traditional roles in fetching water, cooking, childcare, and caring for the sick and elderly. They are also at increased risk of gender-based violence when forced to seek private areas to use the bathroom after dark. Addressing extreme water scarcity is critical to limiting the spread of communicable diseases in an already fragile context..With FY 2024 funds, the activity will enhance sustainable access to safe water and sanitation, mitigating the impact of communicable diseases on vulnerable Yemenis in conflict-affected areas. Funding will support the rehabilitation of WASH facilities in schools, encouraging children and youth to remain in school and reducing the risk of early marriage or recruitment into armed groups. School interventions will also provide facilities that accommodate people with disabilities, helping eliminate bias and stigma while ensuring equal access for all..The project will rehabilitate water and sanitation networks, improving service delivery to the most vulnerable communities. These interventions will focus on internally displaced person communities addressing issues like overflowing sewage systems. Hygiene awareness training will remain an integral part of the program, promoting better health outcomes. Additionally, funds will be used to strengthen the capacity of local water authorities to manage WASH facilities by providing them with essential tools to maintain facilities beyond U.S. Government investments. Most importantly, the program goes beyond service delivery by addressing issues related to safety, security, dignity, and community climate resilience....

description.narrative: (Yemen): .Yemen's Systems, Health and Resilience Project (SHARP) is based on trust-building, self-reliance, and increased resilience to support stabilization efforts, strengthen systems, and engage local institutions to create the conditions for sustainability. SHARP, USAID's three-year flagship health activity, will take an integrated approach to reducing maternal, newborn, and child morbidity and mortality by focusing on the Minimum Service Package (MSP), emphasizing integrated reproductive, maternal and neonatal and child health (RMNCH) services, coupled with appropriate wrap-around support services that address life-threatening challenges for communities (e.g. malnutrition, cholera, diarrhea) with strong community engagement to change health seeking behaviors and health systems strengthening activities to create local ownership to sustain system enhancements post-project. SHARP will continue to foster an enabling environment and strengthen the health system by improving policies, strategies, practices, and increasing local ownership. ..With FY21 funds, SHARP will continue implementing core project activities launched last year in target governorates. SHARP will promote community outreach and engagement with quality, evidence-based messages via direct community engagement with local leaders and health care workers as well as media to introduce and reinforce key messages via community health counseling and services. SHARP will continue working both in the community with the help of the community midwives (CMWs) and the community reproductive health volunteers (CRHVs) and in the healthcare facilities to increase the availability of the MSP in targeted districts through a robust referral system and will continue the piloting of a subsidized voucher program and community-pooled savings plan. SHARP will also continue providing high-quality in-service training, implementing Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI), and strengthening management systems. .

description.narrative: (Yemen): USAID's Gateway to Education Program supports Yemen's Transition Education Plan-a national policy instrument developed as a multi-stakeholder plan to maintain progress towards literacy and longer-term educational goals in Yemen. Through Gateway, USAID aims to increase access to quality education in Yemen where nearly two million children are out of school and most lack basic services such as clean water and nutrition due to a protracted seven-year conflict...With FY 2022 education-earmarked funds, it is anticipated that the activity will 1) Develop, produce and distribute teaching and learning materials for grade 1-3 literacy and mathematics, including reviewing, updating, and adapting previously developed materials; 2) Integrate current efforts to educate out-of-school children (OOSC) through non-formal education and to prevent dropout through remedial educational programs with efforts to strengthen the formal school system (i.e. supporting entry and retention in the formal system for OOSC); 3) Work with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to provide teacher development and training to strengthen education service delivery; 4) Facilitate the involvement of families and communities in supporting their children's education; 5) Rehabilitate and equip learning spaces to support improved education provision; and 6) Increase access for vulnerable groups including support for children with disabilities, girls, and conflict affected youth and their families..Activities will result in a strengthened, more resilient education system that provides a range of services to meet the complex learning needs of the children of Yemen, many of whom have experienced disruptions to their education during the ongoing conflict. The activities directly contribute to USAID's 2018 Global Education Policy and the priorities of the MOE as laid out in its Transition Education Plan..

title.narrative: Yemen Continuous Learning and Evaluation Activity (YCLE)

description.narrative: (Yemen): The Yemen Continuous Learning and Evaluation activity (YCLE) is USAID/Yemen's monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) contract, providing a range of third-party monitoring, evaluation, and other analytical services across the portfolio. With FY 2024 funds, YCLE will conduct third party monitoring of mission activities, contextual monitoring (as needed), and other analytical services needed to support the Mission's implementation and oversight of activity implementation. YCLE will utilize a "virtual tour" tool to monitor interventions in the more non-permissive geographical areas where there is USAID programming. Assessments and evaluations will be conducted as demand requires to support Mission learning needs. YCLE will also work to strengthen implementing partner activity monitoring and reporting and to support Mission MEL needs, including setting realistic but ambitious targets and reporting accurate results. ..

description.narrative: (Yemen): With FY 2024 funds, the activity will strengthen the resistance of communities to trafficking and recruitment-especially of children-into armed groups; the activity will support the reintegration of Children Associated with Armed Forces and Armed Groups (CAAFAG) and former combatants back into local communities through individual assistance and community-based support. Interventions under this Program will address a broad range of community, family, and individual needs, including the conflict resolution and reconciliation; support to education, vocational training, and income generation/livelihood opportunities; and the creation of safe spaces and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) centers. All interventions will prioritize support to vulnerable population groups including children, adolescents, women, and marginalized groups and will enhance transparency and human rights, with a special emphasis on protection from sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). Interventions include raising awareness of the CAAFAG issue, discussing how to address this threat through child protection mechanisms, early warning systems, service delivery and referral networks, and stakeholders' partnerships. .The activity will support community structures and community-based/civil society organizations to lead prevention mechanisms and support services for CAAFAG reintegration thereby advancing peacebuilding and reconciliation at the local level. Interventions align with the key objectives of the USG Strategy on Women, Peace and Security (WPS): (i) women are more prepared and increasingly able to participate meaningfully in civic and political leadership, in decision-making processes, and in institutions to promote peace and security; and (ii) women and girls have their rights protected and GBV prevention and response in conflict and crisis contexts is strengthened..Of these funds, $450,000 will go towards the Marla Ruzicka earmark.....

description.narrative: (Yemen): With FY2024 funds, Strengthening Healthcare Access in Yemen will deepen healthcare coverage and service quality. It will strengthen referral networks for higher levels of Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (RMNCH) care, increase access to and quality of family planning services, strengthen district and local level health governance and healthcare quality and expand community-based approaches to reach vulnerable populations, with the goal of reducing mortality among women of reproductive age, their newborns and children under five as well as increasing community and health system resilience. .The activity will focus on interventions that optimize RMNCH outcomes, taking an integrated approach by focusing on the Minimum Service Package (MSP). This will be coupled with appropriate support services that address life-threatening challenges for communities (e.g. malnutrition, cholera, diarrhea), including immunization and family planning, and encourage strong community engagement to improve health seeking behaviors and strengthen health systems to create local ownership to sustain system enhancements post-project. .The activity will promote community outreach and engagement with quality, evidence-based messages via direct community engagement with local leaders and health care workers as well as media to introduce and reinforce key messages via community health counseling and services. It will work in the community with the help of community midwives (CMWs) and in health care facilities to increase the availability of the MSP in targeted districts through a robust referral system. It will also build the skills of those midwives and strengthen their links to health care facilities. .The activity will also support sustainable health system improvements through building health management information systems that support better decision-making at the district and national levels....

title.narrative: [Redacted] Provision of Information Management SUpport to Yemen Crisis Response Clusters

description.narrative: The project aims to provide Information Management (IM) support to clusters responding to the Yemen crisis. The project provides IM support and coordination services, including cluster/sector lead agencies, and approximately 130 active organizations encompassing other international agencies and nongovernmental organizations (NGOs). [Redacted] direct support to core coordination mechanisms has contributed to enhancing cross-hub operations as well as better information-sharing amongst clusters by providing IM tools that enable situational awareness and common analysis to guide decision making and inform sectoral and inter-sectoral response planning.

description.narrative: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

description.narrative: Support and strengthen the negotiation process and implement peace and reconciliation processes, accords and ceasefire agreements at track levels 1, 2 and 3, including support to indigenous peacebuilding efforts. For a peace/negotiations process to have a chance of success, it must entail building trust in the process, between parties, and among their constituents, with a special focus on including women. Illustrative activities include negotiation training; platform development; public opinion polling; facilitation activities; elder statesmen engagement; provision of international expert advice and knowledge; financial support to parties; multi-stakeholder dialogues; assistance with the design of peacebuilding training programs; support and maintenance of agreed verification mechanisms; support to complaint tracking mechanisms; and work with local and national government representatives to bring them closer to their constituencies.

title.narrative: Yemen Monitoring and Evaluation Project II

description.narrative: (Yemen): FY2015 funding will be used to support YMEPII to report on atmospheric data, conduct a retrospective Youth Assessment, and prepare analysis on data by sector which will be used by to reflect on and amend the current Country Development Cooperation Strategy (CDCS) for 2014 -2016 and inform subsequent strategy changes. ~Pending improvements in Yemen's political and security environment, YMEPII's scope of services to be performed would be expanded to include: overall program performance analyses, project and activity-level performance monitoring and evaluation services, as well as prerequisite planning, systems development and management, training and orientation, and outreach and communications support services. ~Services are to be provided in collaboration with USAID/Yemen program implementing partners. ~The objective is to advance collaboration and learning that will impact future programming as much as drive necessary adaptations in response to a highly complex and often restrictive operating environment.

description.narrative: (Yemen): .This activity assists local governments in Yemen to respond to conflict-affected populations through improved delivery of services by helping the Social Fund for Development, a key Yemeni institution, implement activities. Funds bolster support for local institutions through re-starting economic activity and employment. Funding supports targeted governorates through providing skills for employment in education for women and youth and increase capacity of community midwives and paramedics. Additionally, $4.3 million is designated for agricultural livelihood support for fishermen and coffee farmers through training related to new technologies and techniques and provision of equipment and tools to increase productivity. Funds build SFD capacity of program oversight reporting and quality assurance to ensure local institutions can continue to provide services for improved and expanded employment generating activities.........

description.narrative: (Yemen): This USAID supported intervention will make significant impact to ongoing education activities in a very difficult situation across the country. Providing continuous support to bridge critical gaps in the Education Response to the crisis, the activity targets the most vulnerable, affected children with particular focus on areas with IDP children. This project restores access and re-entry to basic education with UNICEF and the Ministry of Education (MoE) through Back-to-School Programs (60,000 students are receiving school bags and basic learning supplies), support to administer year-end exams Grade 9 and 12, a Safer School project (planned for 11 governorates), minor physical rehabilitation of schools (200 schools), self-learning (15,000 students targeted) and psychosocial support.

title.narrative: Yemen-Maternal and Child Health Integrated Project (Y-MCHIP), Phase-II

description.narrative: (Yemen): Using FY15 funding, USAID/Yemen MCHIP (Y-MCHIP) will strengthen the Ministry of Public Health and Population's (MoPHP) maternal and ~reproductive and child and reproductive health ~systems and seek to improve health seeking behavior at both the household and facility levels. ~Programming will respond to dramatically deteriorated health sector systems and elevated needs at the central and governorate levels, following necessary assessments by MCHIP, including a needs assessments and gap analysis on maternal, nutrition, and child health. ~MCHIP will provide family planning and reproductive health care services at the household and at the governmental and private facility service levels. ~Y-MCHIP is a five year bilateral-award that will apply innovative, high-impact sustainable best practices designed to reduce preventable maternal and child deaths.

title.narrative: Technical and Operational Assistance in Support of USAIDs Yemen Stabilization Initiative (YSI)

description.narrative: Under this Task Order, the first awarded under the USAID Support that Augments Rapid Transitions Indefinite Quantity Contract, DT will deploy two long-term Transition Advisors to Sanaa and also provide short-term technical assistance to support a variety of YSI program functions. YSIs program objectives are to help the Government of Yemen deliver tangible benefits during Yemens current political transition and promote public participation and engagement during this transition process. DTs staff on this program will provide programmatic guidance, political analysis, and managerial support to OTI and the YSI Team.

description.narrative: IBTCI is implementing a Mission-wide M&E program to provide continued, on-the-ground performance monitoring, verification and evaluation of the impact, output and outcome results and environmental compliance of all USAID-funded programs. The goal of the USAID strategy is to increase Yemens stability through targeted interventions in highly vulnerable areas. To accomplish this, the USAID/Yemen Missions strategy employs short and medium term development interventions to impact stability. YMEP is fundamental to this strategy as it will test the hypothesis that the development needs of underserved communities are causally related to improving political and social stability. Stabilization is the process of making a country or territory less likely to descend into, remain in, or return to a state of dysfunction and/or political volatility.
